text:
Marathon Petroleum stock jumped 3.2% today to $473.38, capping a remarkable 20.75% rally over two weeks. The surge reflects a sharp rally in oil prices—crude rose from the mid-$80s two weeks ago to $96 per barrel today—which boosts refiner margins and earnings potential. Refineries are running at a healthy 92.7% capacity, meaning the company can process more barrels at higher prices to capture that spread between crude input costs and fuel output prices.

The near-term backdrop adds to the bullish tilt: uncertainty around a Trump administration diesel deal with Russia has left traders uncertain whether global fuel supplies will actually rise, while geopolitical friction in the Middle East (Saudi attacks, Iran tensions, Houthi strikes on shipping) keeps upside risk in crude prices alive. For a refiner, sustained higher oil prices and tight supply conditions are profitable, even if they pinch consumer wallets heading into midterm elections.
